recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a single dead-man watchdog: edna writes a success/fail timestamp to the Synology on every run, and one daily Synology scheduled check emails the user if that timestamp shows a failure or is stale; it explicitly rejects a log platform.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to know within a day when nightly-sync fails without reading logs; Docker and a central Synology log were your suggested means, not the need.
labels.Deleted: Docker platform and central log aggregation.
labels.Bottleneck: Silent failure sends no push alert, so stored logs you never read change nothing.
labels.Checked myself: You told me cron on edna at 03:00 emails only on finish, a 4 day startup crash sent nothing, nothing else alerts, you will not read logs, and Synology can run containers.

note: It is one heartbeat-plus-staleness alert built on an existing Synology scheduled task, not a log platform or Docker service, so I classed it SMALL, though a self-built checker is close to the line.
